description:
'''Exotica''' is a musical genre that was popular during the 1950s to mid-1960s with Americans who came of age during [[World War II]]. The term was coined by [[Simon Waronker|Simon "Si" Waronker]] of [[Liberty Records]] in reference to [[Martin Denny]]'s 1957 album [[Exotica (Martin Denny album)|''Exotica'']]. 

Exotica's sound is characterized as being evocative of a time and a place that is geographically far removed from the listener, largely instrumental and combining American jazz and pop music with influences from the Indigenous musics of [[Oceania]], [[Southeast Asia]], [[Latin America]], and [[Africa]], and frequently containing jungle-like sound effects such as bird calls. However, exotica was not intended as faithful renditions of international music traditions: Denny described the musical style as "a combination of the [[Polynesia|South Pacific]] and the [[Orient]]...what a lot of people imagined the islands to be like...it's pure fantasy though."
